response.text:
I won’t open or change the deck. Based on the running order you gave, my top recommendation is:

- Drop slides 6 (Architecture) and 7 (Security).
  - Why: In a tight 10-minute pitch you need to prioritize problem, approach, market, traction/case study, and the ask. Architecture and detailed security content are deep technical dives that usually slow the narrative and lose non-technical listeners. Both can be moved to an appendix or offered as follow-up material for anyone who requests more detail.

If your audience is more technical/enterprise-focused (expects engineering or compliance detail), consider this alternative:

- Drop slides 3 (Market size) and 8 (Pricing).
  - Why: Technical audiences care more about how it works and how safe it is; high-level market and pricing detail can be summarized briefly or left to a one-page leave-behind.

Either way: keep the core storyline (Why now → Problem → Our approach → Case study → Ask) tight and move anything that reads like a deep dive into an appendix.
